datasets.title: Satellite detected water extents between 08 and 12 December 2024 over South Sudan
datasets.description: UNOSAT code: FL20240425SSD This map illustrates cumulative satellite-detected water using VIIRS in South Sudan between 08 to 12 December 2024 compared with the period from 23 to 27 November 2024 . Within the cloud free analysed areas of about 630,000 km², a total of about 38,000 km² of lands appear to be affected with flood waters. Water extent appears to have increased of about 2,200 km² since the period between 23 to 27 November 2024 within the cloud free analysed areas. Based on Worldpop population data and the maximal flood water extent ~655,000 people are potentially exposed or living close to flooded areas. This is a preliminary analysis and has not yet been validated in the field. Please send ground feedback to the United Nations Satellite Centre (UNOSAT).. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/satellite-detected-water-extents-between-08-and-12-december-2024-over-south-sudan]
datasets.details: This is a preliminary assessment and has not yet been validated in the field. It is important to consider the characteristics of the source imagery used in the analyses when interpreting results. For damage assessments it should be noted that only significant damage to the structural integrity of the buildings analyzed can be seen in imagery, while minor damage such as cracks or holes may not be visible at all. For flood extractions using radar data it is important to note that urban areas and highly vegetated areas may mask the flood signature and result in underestimation of flood waters. Users with specific questions or concerns should contact unosat@unitar.org to seek clarification.

lineage.description: UNOSAT analysts compared VIIRS satellite imagery from 08-12 December 2024 with baseline imagery from 23-27 November 2024 to detect cumulative water extents across cloud-free areas of South Sudan. Population exposure was estimated by intersecting the maximal flood water extent polygons with WorldPop gridded population data to derive affected population counts.
